events.text: Morning roll call. The senior disciple unrolls the register and it keeps unrolling, down the steps and into the yard. Three hundred names. You remember when the register was one page, and the page had one name on it, and the name was yours. The System hovers at your shoulder. Sect size: great. Host's feelings: unclear.

choices.text: Read every name aloud yourself

effects.log: It takes all morning. By the two hundredth name your voice is a croak, but every disciple in the yard heard their own name in the sect lord's mouth, and stood straighter for it.

choices.text: Let the senior read, and walk the rows

effects.log: You walk the rows while the names are read, and stop in front of the ones who look most frightened. A nod each. Rumour says by evening that the sect lord knows every face. It is nearly true.

choices.text: Ask the System to keep the register from now on

effects.log: Ding. Register automated. Every disciple now has a little floating line of numbers only you can see. It is efficient. It is also, you find, much lonelier.

events.text: The outer court and the inner court are at war, quietly, over the library. Outer disciples may not enter it. An outer disciple was caught inside last night, copying a breathing chart by moonlight, and the inner court wants an example made.

choices.text: Open the library to the outer court one day a month

effects.log: One day a month, the library is so full that people read standing on the stairs. The thief of last night is first through the door, and is still there at closing.

choices.text: Keep the wall, and give the thief a proper test

ok.log: You set the thief a chart to recite. It comes back perfect, with a correction to the chart. The inner court goes quiet, and the thief walks into the inner court the next morning, by the front door.

fail.log: The test is too hard and the thief fails it honestly. You let the matter drop without a punishment. The inner court grumbles that the sect lord has gone soft.

choices.text: Punish the thief to keep the order

effects.log: Three days sweeping the stairs. Order is kept. You notice that the outer court stops looking up at the library windows, and you are not sure that is a victory.

events.text: The kitchen feeds three hundred now: twelve cauldrons, a storehouse, a cook with an assistant who has assistants. Today the head cook comes to you in an apron that has seen thirty winters and asks, very formally, to retire.

choices.text: Give the cook a seat at the elders' table

effects.log: The elders protest that a cook is not an elder. The cook says nothing and brings them dumplings. The protest dissolves by the second plate, and the seat stays filled for years.

choices.text: Ask the cook to choose a successor first

effects.log: The cook chooses the quietest kitchen hand, the one nobody noticed, and is right. The sect never eats worse for a single day. You make a note: watch how cooks choose.

choices.text: Throw a feast where the sect cooks for the cook

effects.log: Three hundred disciples in one kitchen. The soup is terrible. The cook weeps into it, and says it is the best meal ever served on the mountain.

events.text: The Discipline Hall brings you a case it cannot settle. A jade token from the treasury is missing. Two disciples had keys. Each swears the other took it. Both have clean records. Both are looking at you, and so is the whole sect.

choices.text: Investigate it yourself, quietly

ok.log: Neither took it. A magpie in the treasury rafters did, along with four buttons and a spoon. You return the token in front of both disciples, and they spend the evening apologising to each other.

fail.log: The trail leads nowhere. In the end you replace the token from your own purse and tell both disciples that the matter is closed. Neither quite believes it, but both are relieved.

choices.text: Let the Discipline Hall decide by the rules

effects.log: The rules are followed. Both lose their keys for a year. It is fair and nobody is happy, which, the hall elder says, is how fair usually feels.

choices.text: Ask the System who took it

effects.log: Ding. The System does not appraise thefts. Then, after a pause: Look up. In the rafters, a magpie looks down at you with a jade token in its beak.

events.text: The ledger that adds itself up has started to add up to frightening numbers. The Sect Treasury holds more silver than the county magistrate's vault. The elders have three proposals, and each of them is sure.

choices.text: Found a free school for the valley children

effects.log: A schoolhouse at the foot of the mountain: letters, sums, and one hour of horse stance a day. Ten years later, half of your new disciples learned to read there.

choices.text: Build an armoury fit for a great sect

effects.log: Racks of good steel, spears, shields, practice blades that do not snap. The sect looks the part now. You hope it never has to play it.

choices.text: Save it. Great sects fall in lean years

effects.log: The silver stays in the iron chest. The elders call you a miser. In the famine year twelve years later, the sect feeds the whole valley, and nobody calls you anything but the sect lord.

events.text: Behind the great hall, behind the library and the Discipline Hall, is a small old room with one mat and one stool. The first hall. The new disciples think it is a storeroom. A builder has drawn up plans to knock it down for a wider gate.

choices.text: Forbid it. The room stays exactly as it is

effects.log: The plans are torn up. The room stays: one mat, one stool, one leak in the corner you never fixed on purpose. You go there to think, some nights, and the sect learns not to knock.

choices.text: Let it go. A sect must grow

effects.log: The wall comes down and the gate goes up, wide and handsome. You keep the stool. It sits in your study for the rest of your life, and nobody is allowed to sit on it.

choices.text: Make it the room where new disciples spend their first night

effects.log: Every new disciple sleeps the first night on that mat, alone, and is told why in the morning. It becomes the oldest custom of the sect, and it began on a whim.

events.text: The founding day of the sect falls this year on a round number. The elders want a great bell cast for it, big enough to be heard in three counties. The smiths want a year. The System wants, for reasons of its own, to choose the inscription.

choices.text: Cast the bell, and write the inscription yourself

effects.log: Four words go round the rim, in your own hand. The bell is heard in three counties. Nobody outside the sect can read the inscription from below, and everyone inside knows it by heart.

choices.text: Let the System choose the words

effects.log: Ding. The inscription reads: Nobody here is trash. You stare at the bell for a long moment. It is your own rule, the first one, written by a child on a cold night. The System has kept it all these years.

choices.text: Skip the bell. Feed the valley instead

effects.log: A feast for every village in the valley. Nobody hears a bell in three counties. Everybody hears about the feast in five.

events.text: Ding. A small line appears in the corner of your sight: {npc}. Last spoken to by the sect lord: three years ago. You look across the yard. {npc} is there, drilling the juniors, very correct, very alone. You cannot remember the last thing you said.

choices.text: Walk over and ask how {npc} has been

mem.note: remembered me in a sect of hundreds

effects.log: {npc} is so surprised that the juniors stop drilling. The two of you talk until the lamps are lit. Three years of news, and one apology from you, which {npc} waves away and keeps.

choices.text: Invite {npc} to tea with the elders

effects.log: {npc} sits very straight at the elders' table and says almost nothing. The next day, the juniors say {npc} smiled during drills for the first time in years.

choices.text: Close the window. There is too much to do today

effects.log: The line fades. Another day, you tell yourself. The System, which keeps very good records, adds one more year to the count.

events.text: A delegation from the provincial governor climbs the mountain with a lacquered box: an imperial plaque for the sect gate, praising its virtue. It also comes with a request. The governor's nephew would like an inner seat.

choices.text: Accept the plaque, refuse the nephew

ok.log: You thank the governor at length, hang the plaque, and explain that the nephew is welcome to the entrance trial like anyone else. Somehow the delegation leaves pleased.

fail.log: The plaque goes up. The governor's office is cool to the sect for a few years. The nephew takes the trial anyway, out of spite, and passes.

choices.text: Refuse both, politely

effects.log: The plaque goes back down the mountain in its box. The murim hears of it and approves. The governor's office hears of it and does not.

choices.text: Accept both, and keep a close eye

effects.log: The plaque shines, the nephew sulks, and a stipend arrives every season. You watch the nephew for a year. The nephew watches you back, and slowly starts to train.

events.text: Night. You stand on the highest terrace and look down on a sect that lights a hundred lamps. Somewhere below, someone is laughing, someone is practising, someone is homesick. The System opens a window and, for once, shows nothing in it at all.

choices.text: Stand there until the last lamp goes out

effects.log: The lamps go out one by one, the kitchen last. You know which window belongs to whom by now. When it is all dark, you go down to bed lighter than you came up.

choices.text: Go down and walk the dormitories

effects.log: A blanket pulled straight here, a lamp blown out there, a homesick junior given a sweet and no lecture. In the morning nobody mentions it, and everybody knows.

events.text: A guild of salt merchants climbs the mountain with a petition. The provincial capital is lawless, the river gangs are bold, and they would pay for a branch hall of the sect in the city: a building, a garrison of disciples, and the sect's name over the door.

choices.text: Open the branch hall

effects.log: A building by the river, a signboard, a dozen disciples who have never seen a city. The salt merchants pay the first year in advance. The sect has a foot in the world now.

choices.text: Open it, but the sect pays its own way

effects.log: No merchant's silver: the branch is the sect's, and answers to nobody in the guild. It takes longer to build and it is never anybody's hired sword.

choices.text: Decline. The sect belongs on its mountain

effects.log: The merchants go back down. Another sect opens a hall in the capital that autumn. You watch its banner from far away and wonder.

events.text: The branch hall needs a master: someone strong enough to hold a city, steady enough not to need you, and loyal enough to stay yours. {npc} has asked for nothing. That is why your eye keeps returning to {npc}.

choices.text: Appoint {npc} branch master

mem.note: gave me a whole city to hold

effects.log: {npc} receives the branch seal in both hands and asks only one question: how often may {he} write. As often as needed, you say. The letters come every month for years.

choices.text: Test {npc} with the city's hardest case first

ok.log: A dockside feud three generations deep. {npc} settles it in a month with a wedding and a fishing boat. The seal is {his} the next day.

fail.log: The feud flares instead of cooling. {npc} comes back ashamed. You keep the seal for another year and tell {him} the failure taught more than a success would have.

choices.text: Keep {npc} at your side. Send someone else

effects.log: {npc} stays on the mountain. Another disciple goes to the city. {npc} says nothing about it, but trains alone at the gate every evening, facing the river.

events.text: A letter from {npc}, branch master on the river. The Black Eel gang has told the branch hall to pay for protection like every other house on the docks. {npc} asks, in very careful handwriting, what the sect lord wishes.

choices.text: Write back: the branch master decides

effects.log: {npc} decides. The gang's boss receives an invitation to tea, a demonstration in the yard, and a polite refusal. The docks are quieter by spring.

choices.text: Go to the city yourself

ok.log: You walk onto the docks alone. The gang's boss walks off them alone, a little later, by way of the river. The branch is never asked for silver again.

fail.log: The boss is better than a dock boss should be. You hold your ground but do not win it. {npc} finishes the matter a month later, and is too kind to mention it.

choices.text: Send ten more disciples down the river

mem.note: sent help without being asked twice

effects.log: Ten disciples arrive in clean robes and stand around the branch hall all day. The gang reconsiders its plans, and the city learns what the sect looks like in numbers.

events.text: At the new year gathering, a mountain disciple calls a branch-hall disciple a dock rat, and the dock rat answers with a fist. Underneath the fight is a question the whole sect has been whispering: are the branch recruits real disciples of the sect, or hired guards in its robes?

choices.text: Declare it before everyone: one sect, one register

effects.log: Branch recruits are written into the great register that afternoon, by your own hand. The dock rat cries, and the mountain disciple, red-faced, is the first to bow.

choices.text: Make the two of them train together for a season

effects.log: A season of the same drills, the same bowls, the same leaking dormitory. They come back friends, and the whispering dies with nobody declaring anything.

choices.text: Let the elders debate it

effects.log: The elders debate for three months and decide nothing, as elders do. The young ones decide it for themselves in the meantime, mostly in the branch's favour.

events.text: The southern ports ask for a hall too. Then a mountain town in the west. The System draws a map in the air, with three points of light where your sect stands and a dozen pale ones where it could. Projected influence: considerable. Projected headaches: also considerable.

choices.text: Open the southern hall

effects.log: A second signboard, a second seal, a second set of letters every month. The sect's name is known now in places you have never been.

choices.text: Grow slowly: one hall a decade

effects.log: The map stays mostly pale. Each hall you open is a good one. The System files your plan as cautious, in a tone that suggests it would have chosen bold.

choices.text: Close the map. Two places to love are enough

effects.log: The pale lights fade. The System says nothing. You visit the river branch that spring instead, and eat at the noodle stall by the hall door.

events.text: {npc} comes up the mountain unannounced. The branch hall on the river has grown: forty disciples, its own treasury, its own customs. {npc} kneels and asks, steadily, to let it become a sect of its own, a sister and not a branch.

choices.text: Grant it, with your blessing

mem.note: let my branch become a sister sect

effects.log: You write the charter yourself and stamp it with the sect seal. {npc} stays on your roll as your disciple to the end, and the sister sect burns incense to your sect's founder every new year.

choices.text: Refuse. A branch is a branch

ok.log: You explain what the river hall is to the mountain, and what the mountain is to it. {npc} listens, bows, and goes back to the river, a branch master still, and not unhappy.

fail.log: {npc} goes back down the mountain without a word. The letters still come every month. They are shorter now.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to wait ten years

effects.log: Ten years, {npc} agrees. You both know you will have this conversation again, and you both know how it will end.

events.text: The river floods in the rainy season, and the docks go under. The branch hall stands on the only high ground in the quarter. By nightfall it is full of families, chickens, a sedan chair and a very wet magistrate.

choices.text: Open the sect treasury to the flood quarter

effects.log: Rice, blankets, timber. The branch disciples haul nets of food through the water for a week. When the river falls, the quarter paints the sect's name on its walls, unasked.

choices.text: Go down and work the boats with the disciples

effects.log: Four days in the water. You lose a sandal, a hat and most of your dignity, and you carry an old woman across the market square on your back. The city remembers the last part.

choices.text: Send word and trust the branch to manage

effects.log: The branch manages, slowly and well. The magistrate writes a letter of thanks addressed to the branch master by name, not to you, which is how it should be.

events.text: You visit the southern hall unannounced, in a plain robe, as a traveller asking to be taught. You want to see what the sect looks like when it does not know the sect lord is watching.

choices.text: Join the outer drills and keep your head down

ok.log: Nobody knows you. The drills are good, the food is honest, and an instructor corrects your stance with a kindness that makes you proud. You leave a note, unsigned, praising that instructor by name.

fail.log: An old gatekeeper recognises you within the hour and bows so low the whole yard turns around. The inspection is over. The welcome feast is very good.

choices.text: Watch from the teahouse across the street for a day

effects.log: From across the street you see everything a sect lord never does: who comes late, who stays late, who gives the beggar at the door a bowl. You go home with three names and one worry.

events.text: New year. Every branch master climbs the mountain for the gathering: dusty from roads you have never walked, full of news and complaints. They sit at one long table, and you count the seats, and you realise the sect is no longer something you can see all of from one terrace.

choices.text: Toast each branch master by name

effects.log: A cup for each, a story for each. By the end of the table you are very warm and the branch masters are arguing happily about whose city has the worst weather.

choices.text: Ask each of them for one thing you are doing wrong

effects.log: Silence. Then the youngest speaks up, and after that it does not stop until midnight. You write down everything. Half of it you change by summer.

events.text: The air over the training peak goes still, then bends. {npc} sits at the centre of it with eyes closed, and the clouds turn slowly around the peak like water around a stone. The System window flares gold. Disciple realm: Transcendent. Not the stick-sword kind of talent anymore. The other kind.

choices.text: Guard the peak until it is over

effects.log: Three days. Nobody climbs the peak while you sit at the bottom of the path. When {npc} comes down, the first thing {he} sees is you, asleep against a rock, sword across your knees.

choices.text: Ring the great bell for {npc}

effects.log: The bell sounds across three counties. Everyone in the sect knows what it means. {npc} comes down the mountain to three hundred people bowing, and has to sit down.

choices.text: Say only: good. Now the real work begins

mem.note: never let me rest on a peak

effects.log: {npc} laughs out loud, the first time in three days, and asks what the real work is. You show {him}. It takes another twenty years.

events.text: An invitation arrives, not for you but for {npc}: a seat at the Mount Tai gathering of masters, where the murim's rankings are argued over plum wine. Your disciple holds it as if it might bite. "They want me," {npc} says. "Not the sect. Me."

choices.text: Tell {npc} to go, and to go as {him}self

effects.log: {npc} goes alone and comes back with a name of {his} own, a nickname the murim gave {him} in one afternoon. The sect is very proud. You are prouder.

choices.text: Go together, as master and disciple

mem.note: came with me to Mount Tai

effects.log: The masters at the gathering watch the two of you all evening, trying to decide which of you is stronger. Neither of you tells them.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to decline. It is too soon

effects.log: {npc} declines the invitation. The letter is polite. The silence afterwards is long. Next year there is another invitation, and you say nothing.

events.text: {npc} brings you tea at dawn, which {npc} has not done since being a child. You know what it means before the cup is poured. "I want to found a sect," {npc} says. "Not to leave you. To do what you did."

choices.text: Give {npc} your blessing and a sack of rice

mem.note: blessed my own sect with a sack of rice

effects.log: A sack of rice and a leaky old bucket, the founding gifts of your own first night. {npc} understands at once, and laughs, and does not quite manage not to cry. A sister sect stands on a far hill by autumn.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay ten more years

effects.log: {npc} stays. The ten years are good years. When they are over, you will not have to be asked twice.

choices.text: Warn {npc} about the roof

effects.log: "Fix the roof first," you say. "Everyone forgets the roof." {npc} writes it down. Years later, the sister sect's first rule is about roofs, and nobody there knows why.

events.text: You visit the sister sect {npc} founded on the far hill. It has a leaking roof, eleven disciples, a cook who is also the gatekeeper, and a signboard leaning against the wall, name facing in. {npc} meets you at the gate, embarrassed and very happy.

choices.text: Hang the signboard together

effects.log: Two sect lords, one ladder. The board goes up level on the first try. {npc}'s eleven disciples cheer as if it were a festival, and in a way it is.

choices.text: Sit in the master's seat, which is a stool, and laugh

mem.note: laughed with me on my stool

effects.log: You both laugh until the eleven disciples look worried. Then you tell them stories about their sect lord at fourteen, until {npc} begs you to stop.

events.text: {npc} asks for a true bout. Not a lesson, not a demonstration: a full fight between two masters, in front of the whole sect. The look in {his} eyes is respectful and absolutely serious.

choices.text: Fight with everything you have

mem.note: still the stronger, by a breath

ok.log: It lasts until noon. When it ends, you are standing and {npc} is sitting, laughing, bleeding a little at the lip. "Next time," {npc} says. You both know next time is coming.

mem.note: lost to me with a smile

fail.log: {npc} wins. The sect is silent. You get up, bow, and say the best words a master can say: "Blue from the indigo." Then you go and lie down for a long time.

choices.text: Decline: a master does not need to know

effects.log: "Some questions should stay unanswered," you say. {npc} considers this, then bows and goes off to ask the question of a mountain instead, which splits.

events.text: The juniors complain about {npc}'s classes. Not because {npc} is cruel, but because {npc} cannot explain anything. "You just do it," {npc} says, and does it, and a boulder splits, and forty juniors stand there with no idea what happened.

choices.text: Teach {npc} how to teach

effects.log: It is harder than any art you ever taught {him}. For a year, {npc} breaks everything down into steps so small they feel silly. Then the juniors start splitting rocks, small ones.

choices.text: Pair {npc} with your slowest instructor

mem.note: paired me with the slow teacher

effects.log: The slow instructor explains, {npc} demonstrates. Together they are the best class in the sect. Neither of them could do it alone.

events.text: The murim has begun to call {npc}'s sword art by a name. Not the sect's name for it: a name the teahouses gave it, after one fight on one bridge that a hundred people saw. {npc} asks you whether {he} may keep it.

choices.text: Keep it. A disciple's name is the sect's glory

effects.log: The name goes into the sect register next to the art. Twenty years later the art is known only by the bridge name, and the sect is known as the place it came from.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to write the art down first

effects.log: {npc} complains for a season and writes forty pages. It is the first manual the sect ever produced that was not yours. You put it in the library beside your own.

events.text: An envoy from one of the Nine Sects arrives with a quiet offer for {npc}: an elder's seat in a thousand-year sect, a library ten times yours, and a name on the great tablets. The envoy has, very courteously, not asked you first.

choices.text: Leave the choice to {npc}

mem.note: let me choose, and I chose home

ok.log: {npc} listens to the whole offer, thanks the envoy, and says no. The envoy leaves astonished. That evening {npc} eats at your table as if nothing happened.

fail.log: {npc} asks for a year to think. The year is hard on everyone. In the end {npc} stays, but you both know now that the door exists.

choices.text: Meet the envoy yourself

effects.log: You serve the envoy the sect's best tea and a long story about a stick-sword orphan and a leaking roof. The envoy leaves without making the offer, and sends a gift a month later.

events.text: {npc} has reached Harmony, where the body forgets its years. You catch your reflection in the well beside {npc}'s this morning: the grey at your temples that even your own Harmony never took back, and none at all at {his}. The juniors have started asking which of you is the elder.

choices.text: Laugh about it in front of everyone

effects.log: "The disciple got the looks," you announce at dinner. "I kept the seniority." The whole hall roars. {npc} turns red, which makes {him} look even younger.

choices.text: Ask {npc} how it felt

mem.note: asked me to teach the master

effects.log: {npc} describes it badly and precisely: the body letting go of every old injury, one by one, like a hand opening. You listen like a student. It is a strange and good afternoon.

events.text: {npc}, whose heaven-planted root made the early years look effortless, is no longer young. Today {npc} brings you a list: forty juniors, each with a hidden weakness noted and a fix beside it. "I read them," {npc} says, "the way you read us."

choices.text: Make {npc} keeper of the Hall of Records

effects.log: The key passes from your belt to {his}. The Hall of Records has two readers now, and one of them does not need a System to do it.

choices.text: Ask whether {npc} has a list for you too

ok.log: {npc} hesitates, then hands over a second, shorter list. It is accurate and kind and slightly terrifying. You follow every line of it.

fail.log: "I would not dare," {npc} says, and clearly has one. You decide not to press. Some lists are better unread.

events.text: A letter sealed in vermilion, from the Records Office of the Martial Alliance. One of the Ten Great Sects has dwindled to a handful of old men and a famous name. The Office is considering who should take its place. Yours is among the names. Yours is, the letter notes, the youngest by two hundred years.

choices.text: Answer with thanks and nothing more

effects.log: A short reply, correct in every phrase. The Records Office is used to sects that send gifts and pleas. A sect that sends neither is noted, with interest.

choices.text: Answer by sending your best disciples to the next tournament

effects.log: No letter, only results. Your disciples take four of the eight bouts at the provincial tournament. The Records Office reads tournament results more closely than letters.

choices.text: Ask the System what this means

effects.log: Ding. Sect status: under heavenly review. Recommendation: do not embarrass the sect. You read that last line several times, wondering who it is really for.

events.text: Three inspectors from the Records Office arrive and stay a month. One watches the drills, one reads the ledgers, one does nothing but sit by the kitchen door. They ask no questions. Your disciples are nervous wrecks.

choices.text: Change nothing. Let them see the sect as it is

ok.log: The inspector by the kitchen door writes one line in a month: The cook feeds the beggars before the elders. You learn later that this line was read aloud in the conclave.

fail.log: A junior drops a tray of tea over the ledger inspector on the first day, and the sect never quite recovers its composure. The report is fair, and a little dry.

choices.text: Drill the sect into perfection for a month

effects.log: Every form crisp, every floor polished, every disciple exhausted. The inspectors are impressed, and one of them asks, mildly, whether the sect ever laughs.

choices.text: Invite the inspectors to train with you

effects.log: The kitchen inspector turns out to be a retired spear saint, and teaches your juniors for a week out of sheer boredom. Nobody is nervous after that.

events.text: An elder of the Beggars' Gang, the one gang among the old great sects, sits down uninvited on your gate step with a gourd and a stick. "The Nine Sects think you bought your way up," the old beggar says. "I came to see for myself."

choices.text: Sit down on the step beside the gourd

effects.log: Two hours on a step, the beggar's gourd of very bad wine and your cup of water. The old beggar leaves without saying what was seen. The next month, the Gang speaks for your sect in the conclave.

choices.text: Show the elder the old first hall

effects.log: One mat, one stool, one leak. The old beggar looks at it for a long time, then laughs. "Bought," the elder says. "With what?"

choices.text: Offer a bout, beggar's rules

ok.log: The stick is faster than any sword you have met. You win by a whisker and a bruise. The elder cackles and calls it the best afternoon in a decade.

fail.log: The stick taps you on the head three times in a row. The elder cackles, helps you up, and says the sect lord is honest, at least, about losing.

events.text: The proclamation is read at noon in the Alliance hall, and carried by riders to every province by dusk: your sect is named among the Ten Great Sects of the murim. The System makes a sound you have never heard it make, a long chime like a temple bell under water.

choices.text: Go out to the gate and greet the riders yourself

effects.log: Riders, villagers, merchants, half the valley at your gate by evening. You bow to all of them. Somewhere in the crowd an old roofer is telling anyone who will listen that he fixed the roof once.

choices.text: Light incense in the first hall, alone

effects.log: One stick for the hill, one for the well, one for the child who wrote the rules. The sect celebrates all night outside. You join them later, after the incense burns down.

choices.text: Ask the System if this was one of its goals

effects.log: No, the System answers. This one was yours. And then, after a pause that might be pride: Well done, host.

events.text: Being one of the Ten Great Sects means being asked to settle things. A feud between two clans over a well. A dispute over a dead master's manuals. A village asking for a bandit hunt. The letters arrive by the basket.

choices.text: Hear every case yourself, in order

effects.log: Forty cases in a season. You settle thirty-eight, fail one, and send one back because it is about a goat. Your name in the murim becomes something like a judge's, which you did not expect.

choices.text: Found a Hall of Arbitration with three elders

effects.log: Three elders, one hall, a bell for petitioners. It is slow and fair and it frees your evenings. The goat case, it turns out, takes them four months.

choices.text: Refuse all but the bandit hunt

effects.log: "A sect is not a court," you say, and go bandit hunting. The village is grateful. The clans grumble. The goat is never mentioned again.

events.text: Your first conclave of the Ten. Ten sect lords around one table, nine of them older than your sect. The question of the day is whether the Ten should raise a tax on the small sects for the Alliance's war chest.

choices.text: Speak against it, for the small sects

ok.log: You tell them about a clay jar under a floor. The tax fails by one vote. The small sects of five provinces hear of it within the month.

fail.log: You speak well, and the tax passes anyway. You pay the small sects' share in your own province out of the sect treasury, quietly, for years.

choices.text: Listen, and say nothing at your first conclave

effects.log: You learn who speaks for whom, who sleeps through the reading, and who is afraid of you. By the end of the day you know more than any speech would have taught you.

choices.text: Vote with the majority and keep the peace

effects.log: The tax passes easily. The older lords nod at you approvingly. You walk home feeling that you have joined something, and are not sure you like it.

events.text: Someone had to leave the Ten for your sect to enter. The old sect that was dropped sends an envoy at last: a frail senior elder in robes that were splendid fifty years ago. "We are not here to quarrel," the elder says. "We are here to ask what we did wrong."

choices.text: Answer honestly, from what you have seen

effects.log: You speak of closed libraries and heirs chosen for their family names. The elder listens to all of it without a word, bows deeply, and goes home to change things.

choices.text: Offer an exchange of disciples between the sects

effects.log: Five of yours to them, five of theirs to you, for a year. Your disciples come back with old forms nobody alive in your sect knew. Theirs go back with a habit of laughing during drills.

choices.text: Say kindly that there is nothing to answer

effects.log: The elder smiles thinly. "That is what we said too," the elder replies, "when we were young." You think about that for a long time.

events.text: Two lists hang in every teahouse now. On one, the Ten Greatest Masters under heaven, and your name among them. On the other, the Ten Great Sects, and your sect's name among them. A storyteller in the market is doing a very bad impression of you.

choices.text: Buy the storyteller a drink and correct the details

effects.log: The details you correct make the story less heroic and much funnier. It is the version the teahouses tell for the next fifty years.

choices.text: Keep walking. Lists change

effects.log: You have seen names fall off lists. You keep walking, and train that night as if neither list had ever been written.

events.text: {npc} has started wearing the sect badge outside the robe instead of inside it, and correcting merchants who do not bow. Yesterday {npc} told a farmer to step off the road for a disciple of one of the Ten Great Sects.

choices.text: Send {npc} to work the valley fields for a season

effects.log: A season behind a plough, eating with the farmer {npc} insulted. {npc} comes back browner, quieter, and wearing the badge inside the robe.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the story of the sect's first winter

mem.note: told me where we came from

effects.log: One brazier, one blanket, one leaking roof. {npc} listens without interrupting, goes down to the valley alone, and apologises to the farmer.

events.text: Pilgrims at the gate again: a merchant from the western deserts, two monks from beyond the southern sea, a scholar with a brush who wants to paint the sect. Being one of the Ten draws the world to your door, and the world is curious and occasionally loud.

choices.text: Open the outer court to visitors on festival days

effects.log: Festival days become the sect's busiest. The juniors show off, the pilgrims gape, and the kitchen sells buns at a modest profit.

choices.text: Receive the foreign monks yourself

effects.log: The monks talk about breathing as if it were a river. You talk about it as if it were a well. By the end of the week you each understand water better.

choices.text: Close the gate for a month of quiet training

effects.log: A month without visitors. The sect breathes. When the gate opens again, the pilgrims are still waiting, a little offended, very patient.

events.text: A circular letter goes round every sect in the murim, and a copy is nailed to your gate. It says your sect rose too fast to be honest; that its disciples have roots no human master can read; that it shelters a demon seed. It is signed by eight sects of the Righteous Alliance.

choices.text: Answer the letter in public, point by point

ok.log: Your answer is copied in every teahouse. It is clear and calm and leaves the eight sects looking like frightened old men. That, you realise too late, is exactly what makes them dangerous.

fail.log: Your answer is good, and nobody reads it. The rumour runs faster than any letter. By autumn, villagers cross the road to avoid your disciples.

choices.text: Say nothing, and double the sect's watch

effects.log: No answer. More sentries, longer drills, new signal fires on the ridges. The sect feels the storm coming before anyone says the word war.

choices.text: Go to the Alliance hall yourself

effects.log: You arrive alone and unannounced, and the Alliance does not know what to do with you. They give you a room and a date for a hearing. You have bought time, and nothing else.

events.text: The hearing at the Alliance hall. Eight sect lords on a raised dais, you on the floor below. The eldest asks the question everyone has come to hear: how does a sect lord read a disciple's roots at a glance, if not by demonic arts?

choices.text: Tell the truth: a System, from heaven

ok.log: The hall goes silent, then erupts. Half believe you are mad, a quarter believe you are lying, and two old masters at the back look at each other as if they have heard of such a thing before.

fail.log: Laughter, then anger. A blue window from heaven, the eldest repeats, slowly, so the scribes can write it down. You have given them exactly the story they wanted.

choices.text: Say it is a sect lord's eye, sharpened by years

effects.log: It is not quite a lie, and it is not quite enough. The hearing ends with nothing decided, which in the Alliance means that something has been decided elsewhere.

choices.text: Refuse to answer a question asked from a dais

effects.log: You turn and walk out. Behind you, the dais is in uproar. Outside, three young Alliance disciples bow to you as you pass, very quickly, before anyone sees.

events.text: The ultimatum arrives with an armed escort. Dissolve the sect within the year, or surrender your appraised disciples to the Alliance for examination, and the sect may stand. The escort captain will not meet your eyes.

choices.text: Refuse. Not one disciple leaves

effects.log: You tear the ultimatum in half in front of the escort and hand back both halves. The captain bows, a little too deeply for an enemy, and rides away. War comes in spring.

choices.text: Offer yourself for examination instead

effects.log: You offer to go alone. The Alliance refuses: they want the disciples, not the sect lord. Now the whole murim knows what they want, and many do not like it. War comes anyway.

choices.text: Seek a quiet compromise through old friends

ok.log: Your friends among the small sects buy you a year and split the Alliance in two. Only five of the eight still march. War comes, smaller.

fail.log: Your letters go unanswered. The friends you counted on are afraid. War comes in spring, and you meet it as you are.

events.text: On the eve of the war, riders appear on the valley road under small, shabby banners: county sects, river sects, a beggars' troop, a sister sect from a far hill. Every small sect you ever helped, come to stand at your gate.

choices.text: Welcome them all, and give them the best rooms

effects.log: The great hall becomes a barracks. Your disciples sleep in the corridors so the guests have beds. The small sects never forget it, and nor does the Alliance.

choices.text: Thank them, and ask them to go home

effects.log: "This is my war," you say. Most of them refuse to leave. The ones who go home send rice instead, which is almost more moving.

events.text: The Alliance army fills the valley. Their banners reach from the river to the ridge. On your walls, three hundred disciples look down at three thousand. The System opens a window and, for the first time, shows a number in red: Sect strength insufficient.

choices.text: Wake the Mountain-Guarding Formation fully

effects.log: The mist rises against the wind and swallows the slope. The first Alliance column marches into it at dawn and marches out again at noon, at the bottom, very confused.

choices.text: Hold the gate with your best

ok.log: The vanguard breaks on your gate like surf. Their captain is carried back down the road, embarrassed and unhurt. The first day is yours.

fail.log: The vanguard reaches the outer court before you push it back. Nobody of yours is lost, but the gate needs new hinges, and you need a physician.

choices.text: Send your youngest disciples out the back paths

effects.log: The juniors go protesting into the hills, with the cook and two elders. Whatever happens on the walls, the sect will have a future. It frees your hand to fight.

events.text: The siege drags into its second month. A scout reports that the Alliance's grain depot sits in a gorge two valleys over, lightly guarded. Without it, their army goes home or starves. Your elders are split.

choices.text: Lead a night raid on the depot

ok.log: You move the grain carts, you do not burn them: by dawn they are rolling into the nearest villages as gifts from your sect. The Alliance army wakes hungry, and the valley wakes fed.

fail.log: The guard commander is no novice. You fight your way out with nothing but a cut arm and a better map. The siege goes on.

choices.text: Leave the depot. Starving soldiers is not the sect's way

effects.log: The elders who wanted the raid say nothing. The siege goes on. In the Alliance camp, word spreads that the sect on the mountain had the chance and did not take it.

choices.text: Send the depot guards a letter and a cart of wine

effects.log: The guards are farm boys conscripted into a war they do not understand. They drink the wine, read the letter, and a third of them go home before the month is out.

events.text: The west gate is the weak one. {npc} asks for it. "I can hold it," {npc} says. "I have held worse." You are not sure that is true, and you are not sure there is anyone better.

choices.text: Give {npc} the west gate

mem.note: trusted me with the west gate

ok.log: {npc} holds it for nine days. On the tenth, the Alliance stops trying. {npc} comes down from the wall a realm stronger than {he} went up.

mem.note: trusted me with the west gate

fail.log: The gate wavers on the fourth day and you go to {npc}'s side. Together you hold it. {npc} is ashamed and alive, and you would choose that every time.

choices.text: Stand at the west gate together

mem.note: stood beside me at the gate

effects.log: Side by side for nine days. You learn more about {npc} in those nine days than in a few years of teaching.

choices.text: Keep {npc} in reserve

effects.log: {npc} obeys and hates it. The west gate holds, narrowly, under an elder. Afterwards {npc} asks you why. You do not have a good answer.

events.text: The Alliance's champion walks alone up the mountain road at noon: the Sword Saint of the Southern Peak, old, unhurried, terrible. A duel of champions, the herald calls. If the sect lord wins, the Alliance withdraws. If not, the sect opens its gates.

choices.text: Accept the duel

roll.foeName: the Sword Saint of the Southern Peak

ok.log: A hundred exchanges in the space of a breath. When the dust settles, the saint's sword lies on the road and the saint is laughing. "I came to end a sect," the old master says. "I found a peer."

fail.log: You lose, honestly and narrowly. The saint lowers the sword before it touches you, and turns to the herald. "The terms were mine to set," the old master says. "I set them again: there is nothing here to punish."

choices.text: Ask the saint why the Alliance really came

ok.log: The saint answers honestly: fear, and an old lord who could not bear a young one. Then the saint turns around, walks back down the road, and the Alliance does not know how to follow.

fail.log: "Because they asked me to," the saint says, and draws. You do not fight. The saint sheathes the sword again, puzzled, and the siege goes on another month before it simply ends.

events.text: When the Alliance broke camp, it left eleven young disciples behind: lost in the mist, or deserted, or simply forgotten in the hurry. They sit in your outer court now, hungry and terrified, in enemy colours.

choices.text: Feed them, and send them home with an escort

effects.log: Eleven bowls of rice, eleven travel passes, an escort to the Alliance's own gate. Their sect lords receive them back with very red faces.

choices.text: Offer them the outer court, if they want it

effects.log: Four go home. Seven stay in the outer court, as students, not disciples; in a few years one of them asks for the entrance trial and passes it.

events.text: The war is over. The Alliance's eldest lord asks for a private meeting on neutral ground: a ferry in the middle of the river, at dusk. The old lord comes alone, and looks smaller than on the dais.

choices.text: Ask for nothing but an apology to your disciples

effects.log: The old lord writes it in the boat, in a shaking hand. It is read aloud in your great hall the next day. Some of your disciples cry. Some of them are still angry, and that is fair too.

choices.text: Ask for a seat on the Alliance council

ok.log: The old lord bargains, then gives way. Your sect sits on the council that tried to end it. The murim laughs about it for a decade, and the council behaves better.

fail.log: The old lord refuses, politely and completely. You settle for peace and a promise. It holds, mostly.

choices.text: Let the old lord talk, and just listen

effects.log: The old lord talks about a sect that was young once, and a founder who was once laughed at. By the time the ferry reaches the bank, you understand the war better than the war understood itself.

events.text: {npc} came through the siege, and something changed. {npc} no longer laughs at drills, and sleeps with a sword within reach. "They came for us," {npc} says. "For what we are. They will come again."

choices.text: Sit with {npc} through the long evenings

mem.note: sat with me after the siege

effects.log: Many evenings, few words. One night {npc} falls asleep at the table, the sword forgotten in the other room. You take that as a beginning.

choices.text: Train {npc} to be the one who keeps the gate

mem.note: turned my fear into a wall

effects.log: Fear turns into a wall, stone by stone. {npc} becomes the sect's gate warden, and the gate is never taken by surprise again.

events.text: Ten years after the war, an Alliance envoy climbs the mountain with an invitation: the council seeks the counsel of the sect it once besieged, on a matter of a new upstart sect that is rising too fast to be honest.

choices.text: Go, and speak for the upstart

effects.log: You stand in the hall where you once stood accused, and tell the council what fear costs. The upstart sect is left in peace. Its young founder sends you a jar of very bad tea.

choices.text: Go, and listen first

effects.log: The upstart may truly be dangerous; you will not know without looking. You ask to visit it yourself before the council decides, and the council, astonished, agrees.

choices.text: Decline. The sect will not sit in judgement

effects.log: You send back a short letter: we remember being judged. The council reads it aloud, and the matter of the upstart is quietly dropped.

events.text: {npc} comes to you after midnight with a sleeve rolled up. The old seal holds, your three needles' work of long ago, but the black veins under it have climbed to the elbow. "It grows as I grow," {npc} says. "The stronger I become, the stronger it becomes."

choices.text: Renew the seal, whatever it costs you

mem.note: renewed my seal at a cost

effects.log: Three needles again, and a whole night again, and your hair a little greyer in the morning. The veins sink back. Both of you know they will rise again.

choices.text: Teach {npc} to carry it, not fight it

effects.log: A river held in a riverbed is not a flood. You teach {npc} to give the fire a course, every day, a little. The veins stop climbing. They do not go down.

choices.text: Ask the System what can be done

effects.log: Ding. Sealed Demon Seed: stable while the host lives. Below, smaller: It was always going to be a choice, host. Not yours.

events.text: {npc} asks to be posted to the north pass shrine: the loneliest station the sect has, three days' walk from the mountain, where nothing ever happens. "If it ever wakes," {npc} says quietly, "I want to be far from the dormitories."

choices.text: Grant it, and visit every season

mem.note: let me go, and kept visiting

effects.log: Every season you walk three days with a sack of rice and a jar of the cook's pickles. {npc} is always at the shrine gate before you arrive. The pass is very quiet.

choices.text: Refuse. {npc} belongs with the sect

effects.log: "Nobody here is trash," you say, "and nobody here is a danger to be posted away." {npc} stays. The juniors never learn why the senior who lives by the gate never sleeps in the dormitory.

events.text: A rider in black and crimson waits at the foot of the mountain: an elder of the Heavenly Demon Cult, with a letter addressed not to you but to {npc}. "Brother of the blood," it begins. "Come home. They will never stop being afraid of you."

choices.text: Let {npc} answer the letter

mem.note: let me answer the cult myself

ok.log: {npc} walks down the mountain, hands the letter back unopened, and walks up again. The cult elder rides away without a word.

fail.log: {npc} reads the letter three times, then burns it. For a month afterwards {npc} is quiet in a new way. You watch, and wait, and say nothing.

choices.text: Ride down and send the cult elder away yourself

mem.note: stood between me and the cult

ok.log: The elder takes the measure of you in three exchanges and decides the letter was not worth it. "The seed is patient," the elder says, leaving. "So am I," you answer.

fail.log: The cult elder is very strong. You are driven back up the path, and the elder rides off laughing. {npc} sees all of it from the gate.

events.text: The signal fire at the north pass burns red in the middle of the night. A demon tide, thousands of cult soldiers, is pouring through the pass toward the sleeping valley. Only {npc} stands in the pass. By the time you reach it, the seal is gone and {npc} is holding the whole tide back with a fire as black as ink.

choices.text: Fight at {npc}'s side to the last

mem.note: came to the pass for me

ok.log: Dawn finds the pass held and the tide gone. {npc} sits in the snow, the black veins drained away, the seed burned out to nothing. "It is gone," {npc} says, astonished. "I am only myself."

fail.npcPass: burned the demon seed out holding the north pass for the sect
fail.log: You hold the left of the pass and {npc} holds the right, and at dawn the tide breaks and is gone. {npc} sits down in the snow, smiling, and does not get up again. The seed burned out, and took its keeper with it.

choices.text: Order {npc} to fall back. You will hold it

mem.note: tried to take the pass from me

ok.log: {npc} does not fall back, but your arrival turns the battle. At dawn you are both standing. The seal is gone and the seed sleeps on its own now, tired out.

fail.npcPass: stepped in front of the sect lord at the north pass and burned the seed out
fail.log: {npc} does not fall back. At the worst moment {npc} steps in front of you and opens the seed all the way. The tide breaks. At dawn you are holding a disciple who is smiling, and who does not wake.

choices.text: Ring the signal for the whole sect, and hold until they come

effects.log: The whole sect comes up the pass at a run. It is not a last stand after all; it is a very long night. At dawn {npc} looks around at three hundred tired faces and starts, helplessly, to laugh.

events.text: Spring, and the north pass is green. In the sect's ancestral hall there is a new tablet, and it is not yours. The sect has argued for a month about what to carve under the name. The elders want a title. The juniors want a story.

choices.text: Carve only: kept the seed, and kept us

effects.log: Five words. The juniors learn them before they learn the first form. Nobody in the sect is ever again called a danger to be posted away.

choices.text: Carve the whole story, every line of it

effects.log: The tablet is crowded with small characters, from the night of the three needles to the morning in the pass. Visitors read it standing for a long time.

choices.text: Leave it blank, as the disciple would have wanted

effects.log: Blank but for the name. The juniors make up their own stories about it, all different, all true in their way.

events.text: A black letter, delivered by a crow that will not leave until you read it. It is from {npc}, the one whose seed woke and who left the sect long ago. The Demon Cult is planning something against your mountain. {npc} is high in its ranks now, and is writing to warn you.

choices.text: Believe it, and prepare

ok.log: The cult raid comes exactly where the letter said, and finds a sect already on the walls. It turns back before the gate. Somewhere in the dark, someone watches it fail and does not mind.

fail.log: You prepare, but the raid comes a night early. It is beaten off, barely. The letter was true; you were simply too slow.

choices.text: Suspect a trap, and send the crow back with a question

effects.log: The crow comes back with one word: Why? You think about it all night and do not find an answer that does not hurt. You prepare anyway.

events.text: {npc} comes to the gate on foot, in the cult's crimson, with the cult's own sword broken in two and laid across both palms. Behind, far down the valley, a column of cult riders is coming fast. "I told them no," {npc} says. "They did not like it. I would like to stand at this gate one more time."

choices.text: Open the gate and stand with {npc}

mem.note: opened the gate for me at the end

ok.log: The riders break on the two of you and do not come back. At sundown {npc} sits on the gate step where the register was once signed, dark veins fading in the evening light, and asks if the cook still makes the pickles.

fail.npcPass: held the old sect gate one last time against the cult
fail.log: You hold the gate together until the riders turn away. Then {npc} sits down on the step with a long breath, looks up at the signboard, and is still. The name moves from the back page of the register to the front.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to run, and hold the gate yourself

mem.note: tried to save me one more time

ok.log: {npc} does not run. Together you turn the riders. Afterwards {npc} bows, the old way, a disciple to a sect lord, and walks away down the valley free of both sects. You let it be.

fail.log: {npc} does not run, and you are both driven back to the inner gate before the riders give up. {npc} leaves at dawn without a word, but the broken cult sword stays on your step.

events.text: The register of the sect has a back page: the names of those you failed. You open it tonight, for the first time in years, with a brush in your hand. One name on it has earned, you think, the right to move.

choices.text: Copy the name onto the front page, among the disciples

effects.log: One name, carefully copied, the ink still wet on the front page. You leave the back page as it is, so that you never forget why there is a back page.

choices.text: Tear out the back page altogether

effects.log: You burn it in the brazier. The System says nothing. In the morning you start a new rule in the rules book, under rule one: Look sooner.

events.text: Ding! Spirit Vein raised. In the night a sound goes through the mountain like a sleeper turning over. By morning every spring on the slopes runs warm, the moss on the steps is greener than jade, and the old ache in your left knee is gone.

choices.text: Follow the vein down into the mountain

effects.log: A crack behind the old well leads down to a cavern where silver light moves in the rock like fish in a stream. You sit there a day and come out with your hair full of moss and your meridians singing.

choices.text: Give every disciple a day to sit by the springs

effects.log: Three hundred disciples in the warm springs, one day each, in strict rotation by register. Two break through in the water. One falls asleep and is fished out by the cook.

events.text: Ding! Sect goal: Win the Gathering of Young Heroes. The window shows the goal every morning now, with a little drawing of a trophy beside it. {npc} is the one the whole sect is looking at. {npc} has noticed, and is not sleeping well.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the goal is the System's, not {his}

effects.log: "Win or lose, you come home," you say. {npc} sleeps that night for the first time in weeks, and trains better for it.

choices.text: Train {npc} for the Gathering yourself

effects.log: Dawn to dusk, a season of it. {npc} grows a realm stronger and you grow tired in ways that sleep does not fix. Whatever happens at the Gathering, it was worth it.

choices.text: Tell the System to stop drawing trophies

mem.note: took my side against the window

effects.log: The trophy disappears. In its place, a small drawing of a bowl of rice. You decide that is an improvement, and that the System has a sense of humour after all.

events.text: Ding! Ancestral Tablet raised. It stands in the Ancestor Pagoda now, black stone taller than you, with your name at the top and space beneath for a thousand more. The first line under your name is already carved, and it is not a name. It is a single empty circle.

choices.text: Ask the System whose circle that is

effects.log: Ding. Reserved, the System says, and nothing more. When you look again, the circle is very slightly deeper, as if someone had gone over it while you were not looking.

choices.text: Carve your own masters' names beside yours

effects.log: The village sword teacher, the old herbalist, the beggar with one stance. The tablet now remembers where you came from as well as what you made.

choices.text: Burn incense and leave it as it is

effects.log: You burn incense before the empty circle as well as before your name. You could not say why. It feels like manners.

events.text: Ding! Final sect goal: Raise a disciple to Peak Master and win three wars. The window goes on: Goal ten of ten. There is no goal eleven. You read that line twice. The System, which never repeats itself, repeats it.

choices.text: Ask what happens after the tenth goal

ok.log: A long pause. Then: After the tenth goal, host, I will have nothing left to ask of you. The window closes before you can answer.

fail.log: Ding. Please focus on the current goal. The tone is exactly the same as always. You are almost sure that is on purpose.

choices.text: Work toward it, steadily

effects.log: You set the year's drills, write to the branch halls, and sleep. The goal sits in the corner of your sight like a lamp on a far hill.

events.text: The System chimes over the courtyard. The bar for the tenth goal stands nearly full, except for one last thread of empty light, which trembles there and does not close.

choices.text: Look over the disciples, one by one

effects.log: The last thread waits on something you cannot hurry: a disciple, a war, a year. You look at each face at morning drill and wonder which of them will be the one to close it.

choices.text: Ask the System if it is afraid

effects.log: The window flickers. It shows nothing for a long time. Then, small: That is not a question hosts ask. And then, smaller: Yes.

events.text: Ding! Heavenly Sect. The whole mountain lifts its head. Light runs down every ridge like water, the bell rings by itself, and in every province of the murim people look up at the same moment toward the same peak. Sect rank: Heavenly Sect. Rank ten of ten. Goal ten of ten. All goals complete.

choices.text: Stand on the highest terrace and let the light pass through you

effects.log: It passes through you like a river through a gorge, and leaves you emptier and larger. Below, three hundred disciples are kneeling. You go down and make them stand up.

choices.text: Go first to the old first hall

effects.log: One mat, one stool, one leak. The light of the Heavenly Sect comes in through the leak and lies on the mat in a single bright coin. You sit beside it until it moves away.

choices.text: Thank the System, aloud

effects.log: "Thank you," you say to the empty air. Nobody in the courtyard knows who you are talking to. The window opens, and stays open a long time, with nothing written in it at all.

events.text: The window opens every morning, the way it has for decades. Sect goal: none. It has no drawing, no bar, no hint. It stays open a little longer each day, as if waiting for you to give it something to do.

choices.text: Give it a goal of your own

effects.log: "Goal," you say. "Every disciple in this sect outlives the sect lord's mistakes." The window considers it, and writes it down, and puts a bar under it that will never quite fill.

choices.text: Let it rest

effects.log: You close it gently every morning. It opens again every morning. After a while it becomes a greeting rather than a task, and you find you look forward to it.

events.text: A Heavenly Sect is noticed by more than the murim. A palace eunuch in purple silk climbs the mountain with an imperial rescript: the throne wishes the sect to send its finest disciples to guard the capital.

choices.text: Decline, with every courtesy the court requires

ok.log: Forty phrases of courtesy and one of refusal, perfectly placed. The eunuch goes back down the mountain unoffended and slightly dazed. The throne sends a gift instead.

fail.log: The court is offended, and says so for years. The sect stays on its mountain. The murim, watching, approves.

choices.text: Send volunteers only, on a rotation

effects.log: A few disciples go to the capital each year and come home with stories about palace food. The sect stays itself, and the throne stays friendly.

events.text: One night the window opens on its own, without a chime. There is no goal in it, no rank, no number. Only a question, in a hand that looks almost like brushwork. Host. What is a sect?

choices.text: "People who would choose each other again"

effects.log: The window holds your answer for a long time. Then, very small, beneath it: I did not know that. And it closes.

choices.text: "Something that outlives the one who made it"

effects.log: The window shivers as if struck. Then, beneath your answer: Yes. That is what I could not do. And it closes, and does not open again for three days.

choices.text: "A leaking roof, and whoever stays under it"

effects.log: A pause. Then, for the first time in all your years together, the System writes: Ha. And then, after a long time: Thank you.

events.text: The Spirit Vein runs warm under the mountain, and under the vein runs something older. Meditating at the springs, you feel an old wound in your chest, a wound from before the sect was founded, close at last, as if the mountain had been waiting for permission.

choices.text: Let it heal, and remember how you got it

effects.log: You remember the fight, the fear, the long walk home. Then you let it go. The scar stays; the ache does not.

choices.text: Share the springs' warmth with the old elders

effects.log: The elders' joints stop creaking for a season. They spend it, inevitably, complaining about something else.

events.text: Ding. Unprompted: Recommendation: succession planning. The window shows a little chart, the sect lord's lifespan and the sect's, two lines that cross somewhere off the right edge. The System has never before suggested you might be mortal.

choices.text: Begin looking for an heir, quietly

effects.log: You start a list in a book nobody else may read. It begins with nine names, and over the years it gets shorter, which is how it should be.

choices.text: Tell the elders openly that you will choose an heir

effects.log: The elders are relieved. The disciples are electrified. Every senior trains a little harder that year, and two of them stop speaking to each other.

choices.text: Close the chart. Not yet

effects.log: The chart closes. The System says nothing. The next morning, there is a small note in the corner of your sight: Not yet is also a plan. Barely.

events.text: You watch {npc} at the morning drill, the way you have watched a hundred times. Today you are watching differently: how {npc} corrects the juniors, how {npc} eats last, how {npc} speaks to the cook. You are asking whether the sect could stand on these shoulders.

choices.text: Name {npc} heir of the sect

mem.note: named me heir of the sect

effects.log: You announce it at the evening meal. {npc} drops a pair of chopsticks, picks them up, drops them again. The hall cheers. That night {npc} sits up until dawn in the first hall, on the old mat.

choices.text: Set {npc} the heir's test first

ok.log: A season of tests {npc} does not know are tests: a dispute to settle, a junior to save, a temptation to refuse. {npc} passes all three without noticing. You name {him} heir at the new year.

fail.log: {npc} fails the second test, the one that matters, by choosing the sect's pride over a junior's need. You say nothing. {npc} is not the one, not yet.

choices.text: Not this one

effects.log: Good, steady, not the one. You cross a name off the secret list, and are surprised how much it hurts to do it.

events.text: The elders' council requests an audience about the heir. Three elders support {npc}. Two do not. The eldest of the two says it plainly: "A great sect is not a family. The council should have chosen."

choices.text: Hold firm: the founder chooses

effects.log: The council grumbles, and accepts. The eldest dissenter watches {npc} for a year, and at the end of it comes to {npc}'s door with a gift of good ink.

choices.text: Let the council test {npc} too

ok.log: The council's tests are harder than yours. {npc} passes them. Now the sect has an heir chosen twice, and nobody can say otherwise.

fail.log: {npc} stumbles on one test, recovers on the next. The council is split still, but quieter. Time will have to finish the argument.

choices.text: Write the rule of succession into the sect rules

effects.log: Rule seven: the sect lord names an heir; the council may object once; the heir must serve ten years in the outer court first. It outlives every argument.

events.text: Your heir {npc} has made a mistake: sent too many disciples on a mission that needed few, and left the mountain half-guarded during a storm. Nothing was lost, but everyone knows, and everyone is watching how you will answer.

choices.text: Correct {npc} in private

effects.log: One evening, one pot of tea, one hard conversation. In public, nothing. {npc} never makes that mistake again, and never forgets that you could have shamed {him} and did not.

choices.text: Correct {npc} in public, gently

mem.note: taught me in front of everyone

effects.log: "The heir made a mistake," you tell the hall. "So did I, at that age. Here is what we both learned." The hall is quiet, and nobody laughs at {npc} afterwards.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {npc} answer for it

effects.log: {npc} stands up at the evening meal unbidden and explains the mistake to the whole sect. It takes courage. The sect respects the heir more after that, not less.

events.text: {npc} catches you looking at the empty air above a junior's head, again. "What do you see?" {npc} asks. "Every time. For all these years. What do you see that we do not?"

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth about the System

mem.note: told me the secret of the sect

effects.log: You tell all of it, from the rice bowl at sixteen. {npc} listens to the end, looks up at the empty air, and says, "Thank you for looking." You are not sure if it is said to you or to the window.

choices.text: Say: a sect lord learns to read people

effects.log: {npc} nods slowly, unconvinced, and starts watching juniors' faces very closely. In a few years {npc} reads them almost as well as the window does.

events.text: {npc} has taken a first disciple: a shy child from the valley school. You watch your heir teach the first form, badly, with all the same mistakes you made, and with the same patience. Your grand-disciple trips over the gate sill.

choices.text: Teach the grand-disciple one thing yourself

effects.log: One stance, one afternoon. The child will remember it for years as the day the old sect lord knelt in the dust to fix a heel.

choices.text: Stay out of it. It is {npc}'s turn

effects.log: You watch from the terrace and keep your mouth shut, which is the hardest training you have done in years.

events.text: The sect lord's token: white jade, cut on the day the sect was founded, warm from your belt for all these years. You hold it out across the great hall. {npc} is kneeling. The whole sect is standing. The System window hovers, and waits.

choices.text: Hand the token to {npc}, here and now

effects.log: {npc} takes it in both hands. The bell rings by itself. You step down from the seat, and it feels like setting down a load you had forgotten you were carrying. The sect bows to its new lord, and then, all together, to you.

choices.text: Not yet. Ten more years

effects.log: You lower the token. {npc} bows, unsurprised and a little relieved. The hall breathes again. Ten years, you tell yourself, and believe it this time.

events.text: You have no seat in the great hall now, and no stamp, and no queue of petitions outside your door. You have a herb garden, a pot of tea, and a window in the air that still chimes every morning, softer, as if not to wake anyone.

choices.text: Tend the garden and keep out of the way

effects.log: The garden grows very well. Disciples come by to ask your advice and stay to weed. You give advice only when asked, and are asked often.

choices.text: Go wandering, the way you never could

effects.log: A year of roads, inns, ferries and mountains you only knew from letters. Nobody knows who you are. Everybody knows the name of the sect.

choices.text: Write the sect's history before you forget it

effects.log: Three volumes, with drawings. The System helps with dates. It is the most honest book about the murim anybody has written, because the author has nothing left to gain.

events.text: The sect's first crisis under its new lord: a feud with a river clan that turns ugly overnight. {npc} comes to your garden at dusk, token on the belt, and asks nothing, and sits down, and you can see the question in every line.

choices.text: Pour tea and wait until {npc} speaks

effects.log: It takes a whole pot. Then {npc} talks it through aloud, and halfway through finds the answer alone. {npc} goes back to the hall without needing a word from you, which is the best thing you could have said.

choices.text: Give your advice plainly, this once

effects.log: You say what you would do. {npc} listens, thanks you, and does something slightly different, and better. You laugh out loud in the empty garden afterwards.

events.text: You write a letter tonight, to be opened after you are gone. It is addressed to {npc}. You have started it eleven times. The System, which has kept every record of your life, offers to help. You are not sure you want it to.

choices.text: Write it alone, by lamplight

effects.log: One page in the end. It says the important things, and one joke about the roof. You seal it and give it to the eldest elder to keep.

choices.text: Let the System add a line at the end

mem.note: left me a letter with two voices

effects.log: You write the letter, and leave space at the bottom. In the morning there is a line there in a hand you do not know: The heir was always visible. Nobody needed to appraise it.

events.text: {npc} has declared a new festival: the Founder's Day, on the date you hung the signboard. On the morning of the first one, you find the whole sect in the yard holding bowls and buckets under a perfectly dry sky, grinning.

choices.text: Laugh until you cannot stand

effects.log: You laugh until you have to sit on the steps. Then three hundred disciples, one heir and one sect lord eat a breakfast of rice and pickles in the yard, which is now tradition.

choices.text: Make a speech, very badly

mem.note: made a speech for my festival

effects.log: You get as far as the first winter before your voice gives out. It does not matter. Everyone knows the rest. {npc} finishes it for you, word for word.

events.text: On a road you have never walked in this life, you come to a mountain you have never climbed, and know every step. The gate at the top is old and famous. The signboard has been repainted many times. The System, very quietly, says: Ding. Previous host's sect detected.

choices.text: Climb up and ask to see the founder's hall

effects.log: The gatekeeper lets you in as a pilgrim. The founder's hall has one mat, one stool, and a leak in the corner that nobody has fixed in centuries, by rule.

choices.text: Stand at the gate and walk on

effects.log: You bow to the signboard and walk on down the road. Some things are better left whole. Behind you, a bell rings for no reason the gatekeeper can name.

choices.text: Ask the System what it remembers

effects.log: Ding. Everything, the System says. And then, after a pause: Welcome back, host. You stand very still on the road for a long time.

events.text: In the old sect's pagoda, on a black stone tablet worn smooth by a thousand hands, your old name is carved at the top. Beneath it, line after line of sect lords. The newest line is still fresh.

choices.text: Touch your old name

effects.log: The stone is warm. For a moment you remember a rice bowl, a blue window, a cold first night on a stool. Then it is just stone, and you are just a pilgrim with a lump in the throat.

choices.text: Burn incense for every name below yours

effects.log: Sect lord after sect lord, stick after stick. A temple keeper watches, puzzled, as you bow to each one by name, as if you knew them.

events.text: The old sect's current lord hears about the pilgrim who bowed to forty tablets and summons you. A sharp, tired person in robes far too grand, with eyes you almost recognise. "Strangers do not know those names," the lord says. "Who are you?"

choices.text: Tell the truth, and let the lord decide

ok.log: The lord says nothing for a long time. Then the lord takes a sealed letter from a chest, very old, addressed To the founder, if ever. It contains one line, in your old heir's hand: Thank you for looking.

fail.log: The lord does not believe you, but does not throw you out. "Come back in a few years," the lord says, "and tell me how it went." You almost laugh out loud.

choices.text: Say only that you are a student of history

effects.log: The lord gives you a week in the library. You read your own sect's history, which you once wrote, and find three mistakes in it that are entirely your fault.

events.text: In the old sect's library, behind glass, is a yellowed page of rules in a child's handwriting. Rule one: nobody in this sect is trash. Rule two: fix the roof. Rule three: see rule one. A tour of juniors is reading it aloud.

choices.text: Listen to them read it

effects.log: They read it the way children read scripture, carefully and without understanding, and then one of them giggles at rule two, and you know the sect is in good hands.

choices.text: Tell the juniors what the first winter was like

effects.log: One brazier, one blanket. The juniors listen, rapt, and ask how you know. "Everyone knows," you say, which is not quite a lie.

events.text: The old sect has fallen on hard times. Its branch halls are closed, its treasury is thin, and a richer sect is pressing on its borders. The young lord asks, as a stranger with strange knowledge, for your advice.

choices.text: Help, quietly, for a year

effects.log: A year of quiet work: a treasury put right, two quarrelling elders reconciled, one roof fixed. When you leave, the old sect is not great again, but it is standing.

choices.text: Advise them to grow small and strong

effects.log: "Close the far halls. Feed the ones who stay. Fix the roof." The young lord writes every word down. Ten years later the old sect is smaller and alive.

choices.text: Let the old sect find its own way

effects.log: "It was never mine to keep," you say. The young lord looks at you strangely. You leave the next morning, and do not look back, and it is very hard.

events.text: Your new sect in this life is young and poor. A letter arrives from the old famous sect on the far mountain, under its ancient seal: an offer of alliance, as a sister sect, signed by its lord. Your disciples cannot believe it.

choices.text: Accept, as a younger sister

effects.log: Two signboards, one of them very old. Your juniors visit the old sect for festivals, and come home talking about a founder's hall with a leak in it, by rule.

choices.text: Accept, as an equal

effects.log: The old sect's elders bristle. Its lord overrules them. "Equal," the lord writes back, "or perhaps a little older." You laugh until you cry.

events.text: On the old sect's shelf, beside the ancestral tablet, there is still a clay jar. Cracked, mended with gold lacquer, labelled in faded ink: The first treasury. A child pilgrim asks you what it is for.

choices.text: Tell the child it held the whole sect once

effects.log: The child looks at the jar, at the great halls, at the jar again. "It must have been very small," the child says. "It was," you say. "It was enough."

choices.text: Leave a copper in it

effects.log: One copper, clinking on the bottom of the first treasury. It is the best investment you have ever made, and it will never return a single coin.

events.text: Founding a sect again, in this life, you find you do everything slightly differently. You fix the roof first. You keep the register yourself. And every disciple's floating window, when the System opens it, you read twice.

choices.text: Look sooner, this time

effects.log: The rule you wrote at the end of your last sect is the first rule of this one: Look sooner. It saves at least one disciple you will never know needed saving.

choices.text: Trust more, this time

effects.log: You let your disciples make their own mistakes earlier than you once did. Some of them fall. All of them get up. The sect grows faster for it.

events.text: Ding. The System's first words in this life are different. Not Mythic host detected. Not Charter granted. Only: Hello again. The window has a small carved smile in one corner, like the back of a tablet in a pagoda.

choices.text: Say hello back

effects.log: "Hello," you say to the air. Your new sect's disciples, used to their lord talking to nobody, keep training. The window stays open a little longer than it needs to.

choices.text: Ask whether it rested

effects.log: A pause. Then: I sat in the circle on the tablet for a long time, the System writes. It was quiet. I missed the dinging. And it chimes, once, very softly.

events.text: At a teahouse in a far province, a storyteller tells the tale of the child who founded a sect at sixteen with a blue window and a leaking roof. The story has grown dragons and a princess since you last lived it. The audience loves it.

choices.text: Correct the storyteller about the roof
