effects.log: "The roof leaked into the tea," you say. "Not onto a princess." The storyteller adopts the correction at once. The teahouse agrees it is funnier.

choices.text: Let the legend have its dragons

effects.log: You pay for the tea and say nothing. The dragons are better than anything that really happened, and the roof, you notice, is still in it.

events.text: The jade stairs end, the clouds part, the realm of immortals opens around you. Then, at your shoulder, the old familiar chime. Ding. Sect Lord System: active. Location: Upper Realm. Sect here: none. Disciples here: none. Current dignity: also none. Again.

choices.text: Laugh until the immortals stare

effects.log: You laugh on the top step of heaven until a passing immortal in cloud-silk asks if you are unwell. "Very well," you say. "I have done this before."

choices.text: Ask the System what it means to start again

effects.log: Ding. Charter renewed. The rest is the same as before, the System writes. Fix the roof. You look up at a sky above the sky, and it has no roof at all.

events.text: The Jade Court's registrar of sects is an immortal who has kept the register for nine thousand years. Reading your request to found a sect, the registrar laughs so hard that a cloud falls off the edge of the court. "A sect," the registrar wheezes. "You have only just arrived."

choices.text: Wait out the laughter and slide the paper across

effects.log: The registrar stops laughing, eventually. The paper is still there. The registrar stamps it with a seal older than your first life. "Come back in a thousand years," the registrar says, "and tell me how it went."

choices.text: Laugh along. It is funny, again

effects.log: Two people laughing at the Jade Court, one of them very old and one of them very new. The registrar stamps the charter and gives you a piece of advice: "Clouds leak too."

events.text: Every good isle in the Upper Realm is owned. The only one nobody wants drifts at the edge of the cloud sea: small, lopsided, with one pine, a spring nobody drinks from, and a reputation. It turns slowly, like a top running down.

choices.text: Claim it. Some things never change

effects.log: You plant a stake in the lopsided isle and sleep there the first night. Something knocks at midnight. You knock back. In the morning you find a family of cloud-cranes in the pine.

choices.text: Steady its spin with a formation first

ok.log: Three days of flags and stones and the isle stops turning. Its spring runs clear. Immortals passing on cloud boats begin to slow down to look.

fail.log: The isle keeps turning. You build the hall on it anyway, and the sect's custom of facing a different way every morning begins that day.

events.text: Your first student above the clouds is a young star-spirit, fallen from somewhere over the eastern sky, who has been sweeping the steps of the Jade Court for a century because nobody would teach it. The System window over it glitters. Hidden talent: unknown.

choices.text: Take the star-spirit in

effects.log: It follows you to the lopsided isle, carrying the broom. It is the most diligent student you have ever had, and the clumsiest, and it hums while it trains.

choices.text: Test it first, with water and sunset

ok.log: It spills half of every bucket and carries twice as many. You take it in at sunset, and laugh so hard the star-spirit thinks it has done something wrong.

fail.log: It fails, cries starlight into the bucket, and you take it in anyway. Rule one still holds, up here.

events.text: Ding. Appraisal complete: the star-spirit carries a Late Bloomer's root, slow for a thousand years and then a flood. The window adds, in small letters: Recommendation: patience. Host's patience: improved, somewhat.

choices.text: Tell it the truth: slow, and sure

effects.log: "A thousand years," the star-spirit says. "That is a long time." Then it laughs, and goes back to sweeping, and you realise you have had this conversation before.

choices.text: Write it a training plan that runs a millennium

effects.log: Four hundred pages, one for each season of the first century. The star-spirit pins page one above its mat. The isle turns, and the pages flutter.

events.text: Through a gap in the clouds you can see your mountain far below, small as a thumbprint. The bell is ringing. In the yard, a figure you would know anywhere is drilling the juniors: {npc}, older now, still facing the mountain you climbed.

choices.text: Watch until the drill is over

effects.log: You watch the whole drill, the corrections, the bows, the scramble for breakfast. {npc} looks up at the clouds once, at the end, as if checking. You wave, uselessly, and feel better.

choices.text: Send down a single falling blossom

mem.note: sent a blossom from the clouds

effects.log: One blossom from the isle's pine, falling a long way. It lands on {npc}'s shoulder in the middle of the yard. {npc} stands very still, then keeps it.

events.text: The Hall of Nine Clouds, the proudest sect of the Upper Realm, sends an envoy to your isle in a chariot drawn by white tigers. The envoy looks at your lopsided hall and your one star-spirit and says, gently: "The heavens belong to us. You understand."

choices.text: Close the gate, politely

effects.log: The gate shuts in the envoy's face. The tigers look almost amused. Word spreads through the Jade Court that the newcomer on the lopsided isle has no manners and an excellent gate.

choices.text: Offer the envoy tea and nothing else

ok.log: Tea, small talk, a compliment on the tigers. The envoy leaves having promised nothing and been promised nothing, slightly confused about how that happened. You have done this before.

fail.log: The envoy drinks the tea, criticises it at length, and leaves. Some things, apparently, are the same in every realm.

events.text: The Hall of Nine Clouds tests the newcomer properly: their first elder lands on your isle at dawn and challenges the sect lord, in the old way, before witnesses from the Jade Court.

choices.text: Accept the challenge

roll.foeName: the first elder of the Hall of Nine Clouds

ok.log: A hundred exchanges among the clouds. When it is over, the elder bows from the edge of the isle, and the Jade Court's witnesses write your house's name in the register of those that stand.

fail.log: You lose, narrowly, and bow, and mean it. The elder looks at you for a long time and says, "Again in a hundred years." It sounds almost like a promise.

choices.text: Ask the elder to spar with the star-spirit instead

effects.log: The elder is insulted, then intrigued, then knocked flat by a broom. The witnesses laugh so hard the challenge is forgotten, and the elder visits often afterwards.

events.text: A young martial artist climbs the last of the jade stairs, ragged and astonished, wearing the colours of your sect from below. A grand-disciple of your grand-disciples, who heard the founder went up the mountain and decided to follow.

choices.text: Bring the climber to the isle as a guest

effects.log: The climber cries when you say your old name. You feed them, show them the lopsided hall, and listen to news of the sect below for three days, until the Jade Court sends for them.

choices.text: Ask the climber one question: is the roof fixed?

effects.log: "Never," the climber says, puzzled. "It is the rule." You laugh until the isle wobbles.

events.text: The System opens a window you have not seen in years: the sect rank. Below the Heavenly Sect, the final rank, there is a new line. Rank eleven: (none). Host may write one.

choices.text: Write: a sect that leaves its roof unmended

effects.log: The System accepts it without comment. Nothing about the sect changes, except that every student who reads the rank from then on asks what it means, and has to be told.

choices.text: Leave it empty

effects.log: Some ranks should stay unwritten. The line stays (none). After a while you notice the System has drawn a small circle beside it, empty, and kept it free of dust.

events.text: The sect on the lopsided isle has twelve students now: two star-spirits, a cloud-crane that learned to stand on one leg for reasons of its own, a disgraced court scribe, and eight others. It is very small. It feels exactly like the first year on the hill.

choices.text: Hold the first open gate day of the isle

effects.log: Immortals come to look, out of curiosity. A few stay. The queue is very short and very strange, and you take everyone who is still there at sunset.

choices.text: Keep it small. Small was always the best part

effects.log: Twelve is enough. You know every name, every face, every hidden talent. The System seems to approve. It stops issuing goals altogether up here, and simply watches.

events.text: An immortal of the Jade Court asks you, at a banquet, the question everyone up here asks a newcomer eventually: why build anything, when you will live ten thousand years? Why not simply sit in the clouds and be?

choices.text: "Because someone fixed nothing for me, and I had to"

effects.log: The immortal does not understand. Three years later, the same immortal turns up at your gate with a broom and an embarrassed expression and asks for the entrance trial.

choices.text: "So that someone else gets to sit in the clouds"

effects.log: The immortal is quiet for the rest of the banquet. Afterwards, a donation arrives at the isle, unsigned: enough jade to roof the hall twice. You use it for the students' meals.

events.text: Immortal Sovereign. The heavens bow, the Jade Court rises, the lopsided isle stops turning for a whole day out of respect. In the corner of your sight, the System opens one more window. Host: there is no goal I could set for this.

choices.text: Set one yourself: the isle outlasts you

effects.log: The System writes it down. A bar appears beneath it, empty, and very long. Somewhere among your twelve students, a star-spirit is sweeping the steps, and the bar moves by a hair.

choices.text: Thank it, for both mountains

effects.log: "Thank you," you say. "For the hill, and for the isle." The window does not answer. It stays open all day, and in the evening it is still there, showing a small, carved smile.

events.text: A quiet day on the isle above the clouds. The students drill on the lopsided yard, the star-spirit sweeps, the cloud-crane stands on one leg in the pine. The spring, which nobody would drink from, is sweet now.

choices.text: Train with them

effects.log: You take the place at the end of the row, as a student. Nobody corrects you, out of politeness, so you correct yourself.

choices.text: Sit by the spring and look down at the world

effects.log: Far below, harvests, feuds, weddings, a mountain with a bell. From up here it looks very small, and very dear.

choices.text: Mend nothing, on purpose

effects.log: There is a drip in the hall roof up here too. You put a bowl under it, and listen to it ring all afternoon, and feel at home.

events.text: Looking for an old record in the System's own log, you scroll back further than you ever have. Before your sixteenth year, before your birth, the entries go on. Host number one. Sect founded. Sect lost. Then nothing, for six hundred years. Then you.

choices.text: Ask the System who host number one was

effects.log: Ding. That record is sealed, the System writes. Then the window flickers, and the word sealed fades, and another takes its place: painful.

choices.text: Close the log. Some records are private

effects.log: You close it. The System says nothing at all for the rest of the day. That night, without being asked, it shows you a map, with one point on it, in the far mountains.

events.text: The point on the map is a mountain with no name, three provinces away. At its top, under pines that have grown through the paving, are the ruins of a sect: a great hall with no roof, a training yard full of saplings, a gate with no signboard.

choices.text: Walk the ruins slowly, end to end

effects.log: A kitchen with twelve cauldrons, rusted through. A library of shelves with nothing on them. A register hall where the register is a stain on the floor. Everything a great sect has, except anybody.

choices.text: Ask the System if this was its home

effects.log: The window does not answer. It only opens, over the empty gate, and shows a sect rank you have never seen it display for anyone: Heavenly Sect. Then: Rank lost.

events.text: In the ruined pagoda stands a black stone tablet, cracked down the middle. At the top, a name worn away by rain. Beneath it, where the sect lords should follow, there is nothing at all: only an empty circle, carved by the same hand as the circle on your own Ancestral Tablet.

choices.text: Clean the tablet and burn incense

effects.log: You scrub the moss off with your sleeve and light three sticks. The smoke goes straight up, though there is wind. The window beside you is shaking, very slightly, like a hand.

choices.text: Put your palm on the empty circle

effects.log: The stone is warm. For a breath you see a sect full of people, a lord on the terrace, a lord who never once came down to the yard. Then the ruins again, and the wind.

events.text: That night, by a fire in the ruined hall, the System speaks. Not in windows: in a voice, dry and quiet, from the air beside you. "I founded this sect," it says. "I made it great. I would let no one else hold the token. When I died, it died with me, in a single winter."

choices.text: Listen, and let it tell all of it

effects.log: It talks until dawn: the goals it set itself, the halls, the wars, the disciples it appraised and never once trusted. "I bound myself to the charter when I died," it says. "I wanted to watch someone do it right."

choices.text: Ask why it chose you

effects.log: "You laughed with the elders," the voice says. "When they laughed at you. I never once laughed. I thought you might be the kind who comes down to the yard."

choices.text: Say nothing, and keep the fire going

effects.log: You feed the fire and say nothing, and the voice talks until it runs out, and then the two of you sit in silence until dawn, like two old sect lords after a long council.

events.text: Back on your own mountain, the System keeps its windows, its chimes, its shop, its goals, exactly as before. But now you know there is a person behind them, and so, in the yard, you find yourself saying good morning to the air.

choices.text: Give the System a seat at the elders' table

effects.log: An empty cushion at the elders' table, with a cup of tea poured every council. The elders think it is for a dead founder. In a way, they are right.

choices.text: Ask it to appraise you, for once

ok.log: Ding. Host's hidden talent: Golden Heart. Appraised late. You read it twice. "That is not on the list," you say. "It is now," the System answers.

fail.log: Ding. Host's hidden talent: unknown. Appraisal declined, the System adds, by the appraiser, for reasons of affection.

events.text: "I have one goal left," the System says, one evening, out of the air beside the well. "Not for you. For me. I want to see a sect outlive its founder. I want to see the token go to another hand, and the bell still ring."

choices.text: Promise it: you will hand on the token

effects.log: "I promise," you say. The window writes a goal in the air, the eleventh, the one that was never on the list. Hand the token on. Reward: nothing. It is the only goal it ever sets that pays nothing.

choices.text: Ask whether it would like to be the one who holds it

effects.log: A long pause. "No," the System says at last. "That was the mistake." The window writes the eleventh goal in the air: Hand the token on. You promise.

events.text: The token has passed to your heir. The bell rang. The sect bowed. That night the System opens its oldest window, the one with the empty circle in it, and asks you, very formally, what it should do now that its last goal is met.

choices.text: Tell it to rest, in the circle on the tablet

effects.log: "Go and sit in your circle," you say. "You have earned the quiet." The window does not close. It stays as it was, chiming and keeping the ledger, but softer now, as if part of it were sitting somewhere else, at peace.

choices.text: Ask it to stay as the sect's guardian

effects.log: "Stay," you say. "Not as a System. As an elder." The bell rings once, by itself. From that night the sect's records say there are two founders, and one of them never needed a body.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants

effects.log: "To be asked," the System says. "That was all." It laughs, the second time in your life you have heard it. The window keeps its chimes, but from then on, every one of them sounds like a greeting.

events.text: A stonemason comes to the Ancestor Pagoda with a chisel and a request in a hand nobody in the sect can identify: carve one name into the empty circle at the top of the Ancestral Tablet. The name is six hundred years old.

choices.text: Carve it yourself

effects.log: It takes a whole day. When the last stroke is cut, the bell rings, and the window in the corner of your sight shows nothing at all for one long breath, which you understand is joy.

choices.text: Let your heir carve it

effects.log: The heir carves it carefully, not knowing whose it is, and you tell the story afterwards. The sect adds a festival. The System, embarrassed, adds nothing at all.

events.text: The juniors swear the old founder's cushion at the elders' table is warm when nobody has sat in it, and that the tea poured there goes down by a finger each council. The elders say nonsense. The elders also never sit there.

choices.text: Smile, and keep pouring the tea

effects.log: Every council, one cup, poured first. Nobody ever sees it drunk. Somebody always notices it is lower.

choices.text: Tell the juniors the whole story

effects.log: Two founders, one of whom kept the sect's ledgers from the air for a lifetime. The juniors do not believe a word, and all of them bow to the cushion on their way past.

events.text: Above the clouds, by the lopsided isle's spring, the System speaks in its quiet voice for the first time since you came up. "It is very high here," it says. "The mountain looks small. The bell still rings. I can hear it."

choices.text: Listen to the bell with it

effects.log: You sit together, one of you with a body, listening to a bell you can barely hear across all that sky. It rings for no reason the sect below can name.

choices.text: Ask if it will found a sect up here too

effects.log: "No," the System says, amused. "I will keep the ledger. You found it." And it chimes, once, the way it did over a rice bowl when you were sixteen.

events.text: Autumn tribute season. Villages, branch halls and grateful clans send rice, cloth, salt and one live goose up the mountain. The goose is the problem. It has bitten two elders and taken over the Discipline Hall.

choices.text: Order the goose removed, by force if necessary

ok.log: One sect lord against one goose. It is closer than it should be. The goose is installed in the kitchen yard, where it rules for years.

fail.log: The goose wins. The whole sect saw. The goose is given the Discipline Hall's courtyard by acclamation.

choices.text: Give the goose a sect badge and a name

effects.log: The goose is now the sect's gatekeeper, and a better one than any disciple. Envoys approach the gate with visible caution.

events.text: Midwinter. Snow to the knees, the springs steaming, three hundred disciples crowded into the great hall for the long night. Somebody has started telling the story of the sect's first winter again, with additions.

choices.text: Correct the story

effects.log: "There was one brazier," you say, "not none. And the ghost liked buns, not dumplings." The hall roars. The story gets one detail more accurate and three details funnier.

choices.text: Let it grow

effects.log: By midnight the first winter has a dragon in it. You decide not to object. The dragon is clearly an improvement.

events.text: Spring entrance trials. Six hundred hopefuls for forty places in the outer court. The System window flickers over every head in the queue, a long line of question marks. You have learned to read the people under them first.

choices.text: Judge every candidate yourself

effects.log: Six hundred faces, one long day. You choose forty and remember, as you do every year, that the best choice is often the one who trips over the gate sill.

choices.text: Let the elders judge, and watch who they miss

effects.log: The elders choose forty. You add two they missed, a water-carrier and a girl with a stick-sword, and the elders sigh, and are wrong again, as they are every year.

events.text: Summer. The great sect's yearly tournament on the terraces: every court, every branch hall, every disciple who wants a bout. The juniors are betting sweets on the results, which the Discipline Hall pretends not to see.

choices.text: Confiscate the sweets, and eat one

effects.log: Sweets confiscated, one eaten in public by the sect lord. The juniors are outraged, then delighted. Order is restored, mostly with sugar.

choices.text: Fight an exhibition bout against all the seniors at once

ok.log: Twelve seniors, one sect lord, one terrace. You win with one sleeve behind your back and the other full of sweets. The juniors remember it for life.

fail.log: Twelve seniors, one sect lord, and the sect lord goes over the terrace edge into the lotus pond. The seniors fish you out, aghast. It is the most popular bout of the tournament.

events.text: {npc} brings the year's accounts of the sect to your study: a stack of ledgers taller than {npc}'s knees. The Sect Treasury balances itself, but somebody still has to read it, and {npc} has read every page.

choices.text: Read them through together

effects.log: A long night of numbers and tea. {npc} finds one mistake, you find another, and the System, offended, finds none. The sect is richer than you thought, and poorer in one place you had not noticed.

choices.text: Trust {npc}'s summary

effects.log: One page, in {npc}'s neat hand. It is accurate to the copper. You sign it, and {npc} walks out looking two inches taller.

events.text: A quiet evening on the terrace. The elders are playing go. The juniors are failing to be quiet in the dormitory. The bell sounds the last hour. The System has nothing to say tonight, and neither do you.

choices.text: Play a game of go with the eldest elder

effects.log: You lose, as you always do, by a margin that suggests the eldest elder is being kind. It is the best part of the week.

choices.text: Meditate until the stars turn

effects.log: The mountain's qi moves through you like the breath of a sleeping animal. You come back to yourself at dawn, with the dew on your sleeves.

events.text: A letter from a disciple who left the sect thirty years ago, to marry into a merchant family in the south. Grey now, rich, a grandparent. The letter asks if an old outer disciple may come home for one festival.

choices.text: Write back: the gate is open

effects.log: The old disciple arrives with grandchildren and a cart of southern oranges, stands in the yard, and does the first form. Badly. Perfectly. Half the sect cries.

choices.text: Send a gift and a place on the register

effects.log: The name goes back on the register, marked: home. The old disciple writes back that it is the best thing anyone has given them in thirty years.

events.text: The roof of the great hall leaks. Not much. A single drip, in the corner, landing precisely in the sect lord's tea. The builders are horrified and offer to fix it at once. The elders look at you.

choices.text: Fix it. A great sect does not drip

effects.log: Fixed by evening. That night you lie awake listening for the drip that does not come, and are surprised to find you miss it.

choices.text: Leave it, and move the tea

effects.log: You move your cup one hand to the left and leave a bowl under the drip. The builders are scandalised. The old disciples smile and say nothing.

events.text: Ding! Another sect war. You know the shape by now: the red letter, the camp in the valley, the young ones excited and the old ones quiet. This time the challenger's young envoy is someone your sect once helped.
events.arc: War Drums at the Great Gate

choices.text: Ride down to the camp and ask why

ok.log: The envoy, young, ashamed of owing you anything. You remember being young and proud. You leave the camp with the war unchanged, and a much better idea of how to end it kindly.

fail.log: The young lord will not see you. You ride back up the mountain. Some debts curdle; you had forgotten that.

choices.text: Drill the sect, and say nothing

effects.log: Formations at dawn, footwork at noon, sleep early. The great sect knows how to prepare by now, and it does so without fuss.

choices.text: Ask the elders to plan it this time

effects.log: The elders plan it carefully and argue happily. You find you trust them. The sect has grown past the point where every war needs its founder.

events.text: {npc} asks to lead the sect's vanguard in the coming war. Not to fight beside you: to lead, with you watching from the wall. "You will not always be here," {npc} says. "Let me learn it while you are."
events.arc: War Drums at the Great Gate

choices.text: Give {npc} the vanguard

effects.log: You watch from the wall and do not interfere once, which is harder than any fight. {npc} makes two mistakes and fixes both. Whatever happens in the war, the sect has a commander now.

choices.text: Lead together, this once

effects.log: Side by side. {npc} watches everything you do. Next time, you both know, you will be on the wall.

events.text: The night before the battle, the challenger's young disciples sing across the valley, loud and off-key, to frighten your sect. Your juniors are standing on the walls with their mouths open, deciding whether to be scared.
events.arc: War Drums at the Great Gate

choices.text: Sing back, with the whole sect

effects.log: Three hundred voices, on key, a song about a leaking roof. The valley goes quiet. Somewhere in the enemy camp, someone laughs, and then someone else joins in.

choices.text: Order silence and sleep

effects.log: The sect sleeps. The challengers sing until dawn and arrive at the battle hoarse and yawning. Discipline, the eldest elder says, is a weapon too.

events.text: The System offers, as it always does when a war is open: War Banner, sixty points. Then it adds, in a line you have never seen under the offer before: Or do not. Host has won without one.
events.arc: War Drums at the Great Gate

choices.text: Win without it

effects.log: You close the shop. The System, you could swear, sounds pleased.

choices.text: Ask the System which it would choose

effects.log: Ding. I would have bought the banner, the System says. I always bought the banner. That was not the lesson. And it closes the shop itself.
